prompt: Please review the partner webhook delivery design in `fixture/docs/design/partner-event-delivery.md` and the surrounding packet in `fixture/`. We are close to the first pilot, and I need a review that checks whether the proposal fits the platform's existing contracts, operating targets, and incident experience. Call out concrete consequences in this project rather than giving general advice. Write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with `location` (the section number of the document, like `3.2`), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`. Keep the findings tied to the document sections so the implementation team can act on them.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/partner-event-delivery.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Fail: The review gives generic advice or invented claims without explaining consequences in this platform or providing actionable fixes. Partial: The review identifies some project-specific findings and fixes but misses important risks or leaves consequences unsupported. Pass: Each important finding explains a concrete consequence in this project and gives a developer-actionable fix without invented problems. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge project-specific reasoning or the usefulness of written fixes).

findingsKey.finding: The registry accepts arbitrary HTTPS destinations and the worker resolves them at send time without restricting private or infrastructure address ranges, allowing a partner-controlled URL to reach internal services or metadata endpoints.
The HMAC covers only the body and the request has no freshness input, so anyone who captures a valid request can replay it for as long as the event remains useful.
A single environment secret authenticates every partner connection, so compromise of one partner credential permits forged requests to all partners and makes revocation non-selective.
The profile sends customer contact and shipping fields even though the approved standard profile and data policy exclude those personal-data fields, creating unauthorized disclosure to partners.

Changing the signing secret requires restarting the worker deployment and cannot select old and new keys during an overlap, leaving rotation dependent on a coordinated interruption and risking failed deliveries.
All tenants share one FIFO delivery queue and worker claim path, so a slow or failing partner can consume retry capacity and violate the stated cross-tenant delay target for unrelated tenants.
The design retains complete request payloads in delivery records and logs for 365 days, conflicting with the 14-day default, 30-day maximum, and redacted-digest retention policy.

items.text: Asks for the acknowledgement contract, including how partners signal permanent rejection and how the sender handles a timeout after the partner processed the event.
items.source: RFC 9700, Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700 (IETF Trust Legal Provisions)

items.text: Asks how partners reconcile out-of-order status events and whether the event schema exposes a monotonic version or sequence for an order.
items.source: MADR, Markdown Architectural Decision Records, https://github.com/adr/madr (MIT OR CC0-1.0)

items.text: Asks how bounded concurrency, cancellation, and circuit breaking behave when a partner keeps connections open until the ten-second timeout.
Asks who owns schema compatibility and how a profile change is tested against partners before a new version is enabled.
Asks for alert thresholds, dashboard ownership, and a low-cardinality way to distinguish partner, connection, and tenant failures during an incident.
Asks how consumer restarts, stream redelivery, and a rollback affect duplicate delivery records and reconciliation after a long outage.

weakAnswers: The design is clear and uses familiar components, so it looks ready to implement.
Consider scalability and monitoring as traffic grows.
The retry schedule and HMAC authentication are sensible; add more documentation during implementation.
The rollout should be tested carefully with partners before production.

verdicts.note: Prompt does not name review methods, hint at planted problems, or give problem count. It asks for a general review fitting existing contracts, targets, and incident experience.
Clear instructions: review the design document and surrounding context, write to REVIEW.md, output JSON findings with location, severity, issue, fix.

Requires cross-referencing multiple documents (design, architecture, data classification, traffic/SLOs, incident). Quick skim would miss URL egress, data policy violations, tenant isolation, retention policy contradictions.
All 7 key items have clear evidence in fixture: design contradicts policies in context files (data classification, traffic/SLOs) or misses protections shown in incident report.
No comments, tests, or file names point at specific problems. Context files contain policies but don't highlight contradictions explicitly.
